## WORKFLOW: General Workflow
KEYWORDS: Endorsement, Trade, advertiser, approval, approve QO, approve spot, change PO status, client, client management, complete spot, fulfill PO, fulfillment
SECTION: Getting Started
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Once a request is submitted, the production workflow will begin. This workflow is setup during consultation with the local point-of-contact when on-boarding at the beginning of vPro use and is customized to the expectations of each firm.
3. Your forms require some basic information to allow the workflow to progress organically. Once submitted the request will require actions to be performed in order to advance to the next steps. For instance, if your firm requires approval from the director of sales before production can begin, then other actions on the request will be blocked until that approval has been met. After production is completed the request may require client/advertiser approval before it can advance to be scheduled and loaded into master control.
4. For instance, in a TV station workflow, a videographer may need to show completion of their task in order for a status to change from "Needs Filming" to "Post-Production". A request in "Ad Review" status will require an approver to mark the spot as approved before it will advance to "Needs Scheduling". Finally, once a spot has been scheduled it may advance to "Needs Billing" and when that job is marked as completed by checking the "Billed" checkbox, the request will then move to archived.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/1500000936201-general-workflow


## WORKFLOW: Managerial Abilities
KEYWORDS: POC assign, QO, abilities, advertiser, approval, approve QO, approve spot, client, client management, complete spot, context menu, fulfill PO
SECTION: Getting Started
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. If you are a manager of any type at your location, you'll have higher permissions and more abilities in vPro.
3. The following are dependant on what role you fulfill, but our roles are very customizable should your job require one of these options and you don't currently have it. Just reach out to our Help Desk!.
4. The various jobs required to complete a request as assigned to a filtered to only staff who's own accounts are enabled to do that task. Someone who is only a Writer can be assigned to handle Traffic or Scheduling, for example. The POC column will show you a drop-down menu for any job your account has the authority to delegate. You can also delegate through the Context Menu .
5. Unassign as easily as you assign each job.
6. The "Add Voice" link in the Files Column will show up if your account has the authority to send out voice-only requests. Full information on this process can be found on the Voice Assignment article.
7. As a manager, you sometimes have to "fix" someone else's errors. While you can click on the client name to open a request back up in the Quick Order view, some fields will be open for you to edit directly from the List View.. Which fields you can edit will depend on your role, but no matter what role, if you can edit the field it will simultaneously lock out other users to avoid and confusion.
8. Typically it is the AE, or through them the Advertiser, that will give approvals on work. However, managers do have the option to Approve or Deny these reviews should they be aware of its outcome.

## WORKFLOW: Tasks and Notifications
KEYWORDS: AI generate, AI script, AI tools, alert settings, artificial intelligence, bulk action, bulk update, clipboard icon, complete spot, email notification, filter by campaign, filter by status
SECTION: Getting Started
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Every user will get Task and Notification reminders when specific events occur. Most of these events can be set in your user settings for getting emails or in-system notifications about. It is typically in the best interest of the user to stay as informed as possible about workflow events. Managers may also opt to lock certain settings to prevent anyone from being out of the loop. Simply click the "Clipboard" or "Mail" icons in the upper-right to open the Task and Notification panel.
3. If your account is set up where you are someone who can be assigned as a POC (Sales, Production, Writing, etc.) the Task notifications tell you when your attention, talent, or services are needed. Each task or job assigned to you may generate a notification that can be clicked on to navigate to the request you are now a POC on.
4. For any workflow event that you've enabled an in-system notification for, you will receive that notice in real-time as it occurs. Just like tasks, you can click on the notification event to instantly navigate to a focused view or "Quick Filter" on the relevant request(s).
5. Every Task and Notification also has a Read and Unread state, much like emails. This helps you stay on top of which you have previously clicked on (Read) or which you've yet to investigate (Unread). All unread notifications show up in bold, while the ones you've already clicked on have faded text. You'll also find an "x" icon to the right for clearing individual notifications out if they've already been read/clicked on. You'll also find sorting and Bulk Action menus at the top for Tasks and Notifications.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360052646573-tasks-and-notifications

## WORKFLOW: Voice Requests for Delegators vProMedia
KEYWORDS: AI generate, AI script, AI tools, artificial intelligence, complete spot, delegators, dubber, find spot, fulfill PO, fulfillment, lookup order, production workflow
SECTION: Getting Started
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Asking for voice work on a production request is started through the "Add Voice" link found in the Files column. Typically, only producers or Production Managers have access to this option but exceptions can be made when needed. Groups of voice talent are most often set up as "Voice Pools" during the roll-out and training period. New groups and pools can be established with assistance from the vC support team.
3. Each voice request can be one of three types:.
4. Starting a voice request will ask for basic information, such as when the talent should have their parts completed and what part of the script they are reading. Voice requests can be done directly, as an assignment, or as more open requests.
5. The "Search Type" defaults to "Talent" which allows you to select the specific talent you wish to voice a part of the script. If you know exactly who you want to use wish to use the search tool to locate the user by category.
6. The filter or search option is always there if you aren't quite sure which talent to pick. This is used mostly when you have chosen a "Talent Pool" that you are unfamiliar with or is perhaps not located at your physical location or building. You can filter based on many voice qualities and properties. You even have the option to play the talent's sample audio to make sure they're the best fit. Once you found the right voice, simply check them off and click "Select Talent".
7. The audition is put out to a voice pool just like the All Swim, however, it allows for multiple talents to upload their voices in hopes of landing the part. This option is mostly used when producers or the advertisers are needing to be extra particular about getting just the right voice and would like to hear staff "try out".

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360056305914-voice-requests

---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.

## WORKFLOW: Voice Profile vProMedia
KEYWORDS: AI generate, AI script, AI tools, alert settings, artificial intelligence, complete spot, dubber, dubber settings, email notification, fulfill PO, fulfillment, production workflow
SECTION: Getting Started
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Users with the ability to do voice-over work should start by making sure they have their Voice Profile set. This is done from the Account section of the user profile. If you do not see this section in your profile, this means you do not currently have the voice ability. You can call or chat the vCreative Help Desk to get this added to your account.
3. Demo File: Upload a short demo sampling your voice styles.
4. I am available for voice requests: This needs to be checked for you to be available in the voice pool. Your name will not show as an option if this is not selected.
5. Include in All Swim: Selecting this will also send you notifications when someone has requested a voice through an All Swim. (An All Swim is a request for a voice with specific attributes. All users with voice abilities that match those attributes in your voice profile will receive an alert to grab the All Swim voice request.
6. Select Tone: all that match your particular read styles.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360050111634-voice-profile

## WORKFLOW: Extend
KEYWORDS: AI generate, AI script, AI tools, action bar, advertiser, artificial intelligence, client, client management, complete spot, extend, extend PO, extend campaign
SECTION: Request Entry & Management
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. For groups and industries that involve a request having a life-span, the "Extend" process is used to keep it active longer. After the request is initially entered, a contract extension or other need could simply mean what is already being broadcast or used can keep going longer than the original end date.
3. The most common use of Extend in the Action Bar is simply updating the End Date to keep something on-air or being active longer than originally planned. As such, the only field that you can edit is the End Date. If multiple requests from the same order and for the same client are being extended, you can also save time entering just one date instead of once-per-request.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360054287674-extend


## WORKFLOW: Copy vProMedia
KEYWORDS: AI generate, AI script, AI tools, QO, action bar, artificial intelligence, clone spot, complete spot, copy, copy order, copy spot, duplicate QO
SECTION: Request Entry & Management
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Using the Action Bar to copy a request is a very simple way to save time by not starting a new request from scratch. This process is most often used for two cases:.
3. A previous request is very similar to what now needs to be submitted.
4. Whichever the case, selecting some requests and clicking Copy will make a duplicate of that past request to then be modified.
5. Clicking on "Finish" will take the requests back to the Quick Order form to be updated. Depending on your group's usage and industry, the copy process will be configured to clear out or forget certain fields. This is established by managers to make sure the new requests being created do not cause confusion in the workflow.
6. Should multiple requests from different orders and advertisers be copied at once, the Copy tool will stay visible until all copies are processed and submitted. The "Undo" button can also be used to back out of the Copy process.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360056075633-copy


## WORKFLOW: Revise in vProMedia
KEYWORDS: QO, action bar, blog comment, clone spot, complete spot, conversation on spot, copy order, copy spot, duplicate QO, edit spot, fulfill PO, fulfillment
SECTION: Request Entry & Management
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. To make sure everyone in the workflow stays informed, the use of Revise on the Action Bar follows a simple path to update a previously submitted request.
3. Most non-manager users will only be able to alter a request that was already submitted through the Revision process. This makes sure that the correct workflow is followed and all the correct parties are notified of the changes. After selecting a request , the Revise can be clicked to open up the start of the process.
4. Each request being revised will need a few minimal changes before they can be resubmitted back into the workflow. Clicking the right-arrow will begin the revision for that specific titled request, opening it up in the familiar Quick Order form.
5. In addition to any changes to other dates, copy, or production information you must supply a new Due Date and post a Blog. The Revision can not be completed without these as a bare minimum. Any new files or changes to the request can be updated while the Quick Order form is open.
6. If you are revising just one or multiple requests, they will each need to be addressed fully before you can click "Finish" to finalize all changes. The check-mark shows up in the far-right column of the Revise tool for the requests that have at least met the minimum requirements of a new Due Date and accompanying Blog post.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360054288294-revise

## WORKFLOW: Reject Request
KEYWORDS: action bar, advertiser, blog comment, client, client management, complete spot, conversation on spot, delete draft, deny request, draft, draft QO, fulfill PO
SECTION: Request Entry & Management
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Using the Reject option on the Action Bar will allow a manager to send a request or multiple requests back to their submitter. The Reject option will only show up if the active user is a manager, but other accounts can be set up to have this option if needed, just reach out to the vCreative Help Desk with your request.
3. Clicking Reject will take the selected request(s) into the familiar right-hand panel for the next step. If multiple requests are selected they will all be shown, and same-client requests will be grouped. To reject a request, it will require a quick blog post. Click the right arrow to reject that specific request.
4. The blog you post should be specific to why the submitted request is being sent back. The "Post & Reject" button will save and post your Blog and return the request as a Draft to the user who submitted it . That user will then need to address the rejection's cause and resubmit.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360056073553-reject-request

## WORKFLOW: Client Management vProMedia
KEYWORDS: AI generate, AI script, AI tools, POC assign, QO, advertiser, alert settings, approval, approve QO, approve spot, artificial intelligence, client
SECTION: Client & Account Settings
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Client names in vPro can be imported from a list provided during your initial setup. That list can include contact information which we will map into the fields used in vPro. We can then lock-down the creation of new clients to prevent duplicates if needed. This lock-down is also in effect when we enable integrations with a traffic or business system to allow it to control the Client names available when submitting a Quick Order .
3. First, a group can choose not to allow the creation of new Clients without manager approval. If enabled, the QO form will confirm the new client creation when a pre-existing Client Name is not used by the submitter. The order can still be filled out but not fully submitted. The submitter will be notified that it is pending approval and will remain a draft until the managerial approval of the new client/advertiser. The managers instantly get an in-system notification and upon approval, the submitter is notified in return that their saved draft with the new Client can now be submitted. Contact your vCreative support team to enable this option.
4. For your approved and existing clients, managers can edit the contact details, attach files, and merge incorrect client information into the correct ones. Under “Settings” in the left-hand navigation there is a “Clients” section.
5. Editing the client lets you update/fix client names as well as general information that hasn’t been collected during the import of clients. Now, your edit includes attaching "Client Files" that are often used over and over for an advertiser. These are then presented on the QO form to be included on a request when needed, perfect for jingles, backgrounds, pronunciations, etc. The File Type available pull from those you already use, new once can always be added at your request.
6. “Preloaded Files” dropdown on the QO form.
7. You start by finding the correct client name you wish to use from now on. When you click the "Merge Into" button you are given the option to choose one or multiple incorrect versions of that label. You will be asked to confirm that all selected client names and the orders they are on will henceforth be under the correct client you selected.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/360051686434-client-management

## WORKFLOW: Appointment Pre Booking
KEYWORDS: advertiser, alert settings, appointment, appointment booking, approval, approve QO, approve spot, booking, client, client management, complete spot, email notification
SECTION: Advanced Tools & Tips
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. New functionality has been added to the Resource and Equipment Management tool that will allow appointments to be added to a request, along with any resources or equipment that might be needed to fulfill the order.
3. As a Salesperson, you can now pre-book a client appointment with or without attachment to a request on the resource calendar. This allows you to “save-the-date” whether for recording of a client ad, meeting for a consultation or for filming the ad. For instance, if a client is coming to the station to record their own commercial or if your production crew will be filming an ad on location, this feature will help you keep all information about a request in one place.
4. If the ad type is using the Resource and Equipment feature, you will see a book icon in the PO column of the list view.
5. Clicking on the Book icon will open the Resource Calendar. From there, you will fill in the required contact information and choose a booking start and end date and time. Then, Save.
6. Once an appointment has been saved, the approving manager (typically the Production Director or Creative Services Director) will receive a notification that a new booking has been added and is pending approval.
7. Upon clicking on that notification, the approving director will be taken to a listing of any pending appointment requests.
8. On the Appointment page, the approving director will approve or deny each pending request. If a request is denied, a reason must be entered.
9. Once approved or denied, the requesting user will receive a notification that this appointment has either been approved and added to the Resource Calendar or if denied, will have a reason the request was denied in the notification center.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/4415562988059-appointment-pre-booking

---

## WORKFLOW: How do I use the Script Template Library?

SECTION: Advanced Tools & Tips
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. vPro includes more than the ability to archive previous production requests and spots. It can also be the home for frequently used scripts in a template library. The script template library is found under the vPro tab in the left sidebar. Once it’s opened all of the saved templates will be on display. New scripts can be added using the new template button. Naming the script is required to add it to the library. Tags and script category may be added to allow the script to be more easily found in the filter. The filter is located near the top right of the script template library screen. As you type the search will update the list displayed in real time. The actions column allows editing or removal of a script from the library. Clicking on the script template icon, that looks like an eye, will allow you to create a new request from the template by bringing up the script time sidebar. More details about the script timer are available in another video.

## WORKFLOW: Lead Time By Ad Type vProMedia
KEYWORDS: AI generate, AI script, AI tools, ad type lead time, artificial intelligence, complete spot, fulfill PO, fulfillment, lead, lead time, order deadline, production workflow
SECTION: Advanced Tools & Tips
---
1. Fulfillment & Production Workflow.
2. Lead Time By Ad Type vProMedia.
3. Submitting a new request always requires a due date. However, the level of work being asked for in the request could better inform the due date.
4. Make sure that simple work can be "due tomorrow" while more complex requests adhere to defined rules by the production department. Your order forms can now have set lead times based on the Due Date entered to ensure enough time between production and ready for air.
5. Customer Support or Users with Local Admin access* can set the lead time per Ad Type or project from the Local Admin>vPro Ad types tab>Ad type options>Lead Time.
6. For instance, setting 3 days will ensure that there are 3 business days between the Due date selected on the form and the first available start date. (US holidays and weekends are not included).
7. A lead time of 3 days** for this ad type means that selecting a due date of 12-9-2022 will give the first available start date of 12-14-2022.
8. *Gaining Local Admin Access requires additional training with a vPro implementation specialist, contact vCreative Support for details.

Reference: https://vcreativeinc.com/knowledge/hc/en-us/articles/5448120146331-lead-time-by-ad-type

Access a request history by using the icon in the PO column. Any changes will have a stricken out version along with what it’s replacing. There are two views available in the history sidebar. You can choose between simple view and full view. Request history also includes a search tool to narrow down what is listed within the current request. You can search by typing in names, dates, and even text from scripts or blog entries. Your recent user history is also available. It can be found in the user account menu on the top right of the screen.
